key_insight: Standardizing prostate cancer EHR data to OMOP and adding NLP plus PSA-based rules materially improved missing diagnosis, pathology, and treatment information.
clinical_relevance: This approach can make routine EHR data more usable for prostate cancer research, registry validation, and outcomes tracking.
method: Converted UTMB Epic EHR prostate cancer records into OMOP CDM v5.4.
Used NLP to extract PSA, Gleason score, and cancer stage from clinical text.
Applied PSA-based algorithms to detect missing treatments and biochemical recurrence.
evidence_signal: The pipeline yielded 815 analytic cases, with 700 (85.9%) complete and concordant with the cancer registry; PSA agreement was excellent and NLP substantially improved sparse Gleason/stage capture.
watch_item: Results come from a single-center retrospective dataset, so performance and data quality gains may not generalize without local validation and careful mapping of registry/EHR discrepancies.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
